name: EXAMPLE
neighbouring_relation: Example-level (U1): D and D' differ in one example of one client at one task. The weakest unit — what most DP-SGD-in-FL papers silently use.
composition_regime: Sequential composition over all releases that touch the example (no special-casing)
relevance: Baseline unit most DP-SGD-in-FL papers use implicitly

name: TASK
neighbouring_relation: Task-level / client-task (U2): D and D' differ in the entirety of one client's data at one task-epoch. Natural for FCL, and the unit under which parallel composition can be legal.
composition_regime: Parallel composition IF the ledger is task-disjoint (flat eps(T)); else sequential
relevance: The unit under which claim C3 / theorem T1-fwd holds: task-disjoint retention -> flat eps(T)

name: CLIENT_BOUNDED
neighbouring_relation: Client-level, bounded horizon (U3): D and D' differ in all of one client's data across a fixed horizon of T tasks. The standard cross-silo target.
composition_regime: Sequential composition over the fixed horizon T
relevance: Standard cross-silo target when a horizon T is fixed in advance

name: CLIENT_LIFELONG
neighbouring_relation: Client-level, unbounded / lifelong (U4): D and D' differ in all of one client's data across the unbounded task stream. What the FCL premise implicitly promises; no accountant delivers this non-vacuously for a client who keeps contributing new information forever (H1).
composition_regime: Sequential composition over the *entire* observed stream, unconditionally
relevance: The unit under which H1 shows every accountant we tested diverges (theorem T1-conv)

name: INDIVIDUAL
neighbouring_relation: Individual / person-level under renewal (U5): D and D' differ in the data of one person, who may recur across several tasks of one client and possibly across clients, under a renewal (churn) model of the population.
composition_regime: Sequential composition over a person's recurring participation under a renewal model
relevance: The unit theorem T2 targets (person-level guarantee under churn), aspirational
